source_text: Ἔτι δὲ πρὸς τὸν σωτῆρα αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰουδαῖός φησιν ὅτι, εἰ τοῦτο λέγεις, ὅτι πᾶς ἄνθρωπος κατὰ θείαν πρόνοιαν γεγονὼς υἱός ἐστι θεοῦ, τί ἂν σὺ ἄλλου διαφέροις; πρὸς ὃν ἐροῦμεν ὅτι πᾶς μὲν ὁ, ὡς ὁ Παῦλος ὠνόμασε, μηκέτι ὑπὸ φόβου παιδαγωγούμενος ἀλλὰ δι᾿ αὑτὸ τὸ καλὸν αἱρούμενος υἱός ἐστι θεοῦ· οὗτος δὲ πολλῷ καὶ μακρῶ διαφέρει παντὸς τοῦ διὰ τὴν ἀρετὴν χρηματίζοντος υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅστις ὡσπερεὶ πηγή τις καὶ ἀρχὴ τῶν τοιούτων τυγχάνει. ἡ δὲ τοῦ Παύλου λέξις οὕτως ἔχει· „οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλ᾿ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας, ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Ἀββὰ ὁ πατήρ.“ τινὲς δὲ καὶ ἐλέγξουσιν, ὥς φησιν ὁ παρὰ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαῖος, μυρίοι τὸν Ἰησοῦν φάσκοντες περὶ ἑαυτῶν ταῦτα εἰρῆσθαι, ἅπερ περὶ ἐκείνου ἐπροφητεύετο. οὐκ οἴδαμεν οὖν εἰ ὁ Κέλσος ἠπίστατό τινας ἐπιδημήσαντας τῷ βίῳ καὶ τὸ παραπλήσιον βουληθέντας ποιεῖν τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ θεοῦ υἱοὺς αὑτοὺς ἀναγορεύειν ἢ θεοῦ δύναμιν. ἐπεὶ δὲ φιλαλήθως τὰ κατὰ τοὺς τόπους ἐξετάζομεν, ἐροῦμεν ὅτι Θευδᾶς πρὸ τῆς γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ γέγονέ τις παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις „μέγαν“ „τινὰ ἑαυτὸν“ λέγων· οὗ ἀποθανόντος οἱ ἀπατηθέντες ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ διεσκεδάσθησαν. καὶ μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον „ἐν ταῖς τῆς ἀπογραφῆς ἡμέραις,“ ὅτ᾿ ἔοικε γεγεννῆσθαι ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Ἰούδας τις Γαλιλαῖος πολλοὺς ἑαυτῷ συναπέστησεν ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὡς σοφὸς καὶ καινοτομῶν τινα· οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ δίκας τίσαντος ἡ διδασκαλία καθῃρέθη πάνυ ἐν ὀλίγοις καὶ ἐλαχίστοις μείνασα. καὶ μετὰ τοὺς Ἰησοῦ δὲ χρόνους ἠθέλησε καὶ ὁ Σαμαρεὺς Δοσίθεος πεῖσαι Σαμαρεῖς ὅτι αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ προφητευόμενος ὑπὸ Μω(??)σέως Χριστὸς, καὶ ἔδοξέ τινων τῇ ἑαυτοῦ διδασκαλίᾳ κεκρατηκέναι. ἀλλὰ τὸ εἰρημένον πάνυ σοφῶς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐν ταῖς Πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων ἀναγεγραμμένου Γαμαλιὴλ οὐκ ἄλογον παραθέμενον δεῖξαι, πῶς ἐκεῖνοι μὲν ἀλλότριοι τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ησαν, οὔτε υἱοὶ θεοῦ οὔτε δυνάμεις ὄντες αὐτοῦ, ὁ δὲ Χριστὸς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀληθῶς ην υἱὸς θεοῦ. εἶπε δ᾿ ἐκεῖ ὁ Γαμαλιήλ· „ὅτι ἐὰν ᾖ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἡ βουλὴ αὕτη καὶ ὁ λόγος οὗτος, καταλυθήσεται,“ ὡς καὶ τὰ ἐκείνων κατελύθη ἀποθανόντων· „ἐὰν δὲ ᾖ ἐκ θεοῦ οὐ δυνήσεσθε καταλῦσαι τὴν τούτου διδασκαλίαν, μή ποτε καὶ θεομάχοι εὑρεθῆτε.“ ἠθέλησε δὲ καὶ Σίμων ὁ Σαμαρεὺς μάγος τῇ μαγείᾳ ὑφελέσθαι τινάς. καὶ τότε μὲν ἠπάτησε, νυνὶ δὲ τοὺς πάντας ἐν τῇ οἰκουμένῃ οὐκ ἔστι Σιμωνιανοὺς εὑρεῖν τὸν ἀριθμὸν οἶμαι τριάκοντα, καὶ τάχα πλείονας εἶπον τῶν ὄντων. εἰσὶ δὲ περὶ τὴν Παλαιστίνην σφόδρα ἐλάχιστοι· τῆς δὲ λοιπῆς οἰκουμένης οὐδαμοῦ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καθ᾿ ἣν ἠθέλησε δόξαν περὶ ἑαυτοῦ διασκεδάσαι. παρὰ γὰρ οἷς φέρεται, ἐκ τῶν Πράξεων τῶν ἀποστόλων φέρεται· Χριστινανοὶ δ᾿ εἰσὶν οἱ ταῦτα περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες, καὶ ἡ ἐνάργεια ἐμαρτύρησεν ὅτι οὐδὲν θεῖον ὁ Σίμων ἦν.
pass_a_gloss: And yet to the Savior himself the Jew says that if you say this, that every man having come into being by divine providence is a son of God, what would you differ from another? To whom we will say that every one, as Paul named, no longer being disciplined by fear but choosing the good through itself, is a son of God; but this one differs much and greatly from every son of God who is so through virtue, who is as it were a source and beginning of such ones. And the speech of Paul has it thus: 'for you did not receive a spirit of slavery again into fear, but you received a spirit of sonship, in which we cry out: Abba Father.' And some will also refute, as the Jew by Celsus says, myriads saying that Jesus speaks these things about himself, which were prophesied about him. We do not know then if Celsus was ignorant of some who had come into life and wished to do similar things to Jesus and proclaim themselves sons of God or a power of God. Since, however, we are examining the things according to the places truthfully, we will say that before the birth of Jesus, a certain Theudas came to be among the Jews, saying 'he is great', and after his death, those deceived by him were scattered. And after him, 'in the days of the census', when it seems Jesus was born, a certain Judas the Galilean gathered many from the people of the Jews to himself, as wise and innovative; and after he suffered justice, his teaching was completely destroyed and remained in very few and the smallest. And after the times of Jesus, the Samaritan Dositheus also wished to persuade the Samaritans that he was the Christ prophesied by Moses, and it seemed that some were overcome by his teaching. But what was said very wisely by Gamaliel, recorded in the Acts of the Apostles, must be shown, that those were alien to the promise, neither sons of God nor powers of his, but Jesus Christ was truly a son of God. And Gamaliel said there: 'if this counsel and this word is from men, it will be destroyed', as also the things of those were destroyed when they died; 'but if it is from God, you will not be able to destroy his teaching, lest you be found to be fighting against God.' And Simon the Samaritan magician also wished to exalt some by his magic. And then he deceived, but now there are not thirty Simonians to be found in the whole world, I think, and perhaps I said more than there are. There are, however, very few around Palestine; and in the rest of the world, his name is nowhere, according to which he wished to scatter glory about himself. For it is brought by those who bring it from the Acts of the Apostles; and the Christians say these things about him, and the evidence has testified that Simon was not divine.

pass_b_english: The Jew still says to the Savior, "If you say that every human being, having come into existence by divine providence, is a son of God, how would you differ from anyone else?" We will reply that everyone whom Paul describes—those no longer driven by fear but choosing the good for its own sake—is a son of God. Yet this one differs vastly and profoundly from every son of God who owes that status to virtue; he is, as it were, the source and beginning of all such people. Paul's words are: "For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you received a spirit of adoption, in which we cry, 'Abba, Father'" (Romans 8:15). Some will also object, as the Jew in Celsus puts it, that myriads claim Jesus spoke these things about himself, the very things prophesied concerning him. We do not know whether Celsus was unaware of certain people who had appeared in history and wanted to imitate Jesus, proclaiming themselves sons of God or a power of God.

Since, however, we are investigating the facts on the ground truthfully, we will say that before Jesus' birth a certain Theudas arose among the Jews, calling himself "someone great"; after his death, those deceived by him were scattered. After him, "in the days of the census," when Jesus appears to have been born, a certain Judas the Galilean drew many away from the Jewish people, presenting himself as wise and innovative; when he met his just end, his teaching was utterly destroyed, surviving only among a tiny handful. After Jesus' time, the Samaritan Dositheus also tried to convince the Samaritans that he was the Christ foretold by Moses, and some seemed to be won over by his teaching. But we must set forth the very wise statement of Gamaliel, recorded in the Acts of the Apostles, which shows that those men were strangers to the promise—neither sons of God nor his powers—while Jesus Christ truly was the Son of God. Gamaliel said there: "If this plan or this work is of human origin, it will be overthrown," as indeed theirs were when they died; "but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow it—lest you even be found fighting against God" (Acts 5:38-39).

Simon the Samaritan magician also tried to use his magic to gain a following. For a time he succeeded in deceiving people, but now I doubt there are thirty Simonians to be found in the whole world; I may even have overstated the number. There are, however, very few of them around Palestine, and in the rest of the world his name is nowhere to be found—the very world in which he wished to spread his own glory. This account comes from those who transmit it, drawn from the Acts of the Apostles; Christians are the ones who say these things about him, and the evidence has testified that Simon was nothing divine.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between the 'son of God' through providence/virtue and the 'son of God' through the spirit of adoption. All scripture citations (Romans 8:15 and Acts 5:38-39) are correctly identified and applied to the relevant clauses. The translation of 'υἱοθεσίας' as 'adoption' in Pass B is a standard and appropriate rendering of the theological term. The historical figures (Theudas, Judas the Galilean, Dositheus, Gamaliel, Simon Magus) are all correctly handled.
